Spatial attributes are geometry valued, and simple features are based on 2D geometry with linear interpolation between vertices. — ISO 19125 --- - A **feature** is a real-world object: a building, a road, a lake - Every feature has: 1. A **geometry** — location and shape on Earth 2. **Attributes** — everything else (name, population, category, ...) - The geometry has a **type** and must satisfy **validity rules** ## Geometry types - 18 types defined in the standard; 7 cover the vast majority of real-world data: ::: {#tbl-sf .cell tbl-cap='Source: @pebesma2018'} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Type |Description | Dimensions| |:--------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------:| |`POINT` |zero-dimensional geometry containing a single point | 0| |`LINESTRING` |sequence of points connected by straight, non-self-intersecting line pieces | 1| |`POLYGON` |sequence of points forming a closed, non-self-intersecting ring (with optional holes) | 2| |`MULTIPOINT` |set of points | 0| |`MULTILINESTRING` |set of linestrings | 1| |`MULTIPOLYGON` |set of polygons | 2| |`GEOMETRYCOLLECTION` |set of geometries of any of the above types | NA| ::: ::: --- :::{#fig-sf} ![](images/simple_feature_types.svg) Image source: @dorman2023 ::: --- - All types are composed of **points** (0D), **lines** (1D), or **areas** (2D) - Composite types arise naturally: a country with islands → `MULTIPOLYGON`, a branching river → `MULTILINESTRING` - Every type has **validity rules** — violations cause silent errors or failed operations --- | Violation | Description | |---|---| | Self-intersecting ring | A polygon whose boundary crosses itself (figure-8 shape) | | Unclosed ring | Polygon exterior ring does not start and end at the same point | | Hole outside exterior | A polygon hole lies outside or only partially inside the exterior ring | | Duplicate points | Consecutive identical vertices in a ring | | Wrong winding order | Exterior ring must be CCW; holes must be CW (OGC/ISO rule) | - `st_is_valid()` checks; `st_make_valid()` attempts to fix - Winding order is **not** checked by GEOS — violations pass validation but can break ESRI format interchange (Shapefiles use the opposite convention: exterior CW) # Coordinate Reference Systems {.subtitle} ## The Earth is not flat - The Earth is approximated as an **ellipsoid**: slightly flattened at the poles, bulging at the equator - A **datum** defines which ellipsoid to use and how to orient it: - **WGS84** — global datum, used by GPS and internet maps - **CH1903+ / LV95** — Swiss national datum, optimized for Switzerland - The same point has different coordinates in different datums ## Projections - A **projection** transforms 3D ellipsoid coordinates onto a flat 2D plane - Every projection distorts at least one property — **there is no undistorted flat map**: - **Equal-area** — preserves area; distorts shape and angles - **Conformal** — preserves local shape / angles; distorts area - **Equidistant** — preserves distance from a point; distorts area and shape - National systems (e.g. LV95 / EPSG:2056) are conformal, minimizing distortion locally ## EPSG codes - **EPSG codes** are the standard identifiers for coordinate reference systems: | EPSG | Name | Unit | Typical use | |---|---|---|---| | 4326 | WGS84 | degree | GPS, global data, GeoJSON default | | 2056 | CH1903+ / LV95 | meter | Swiss national datasets | | 3857 | Web Mercator | meter | Web map tiles (Google, OSM) | | 25832 | ETRS89 / UTM Zone 32N | meter | Central Europe | ## CRS in practice: the silent error - Measurement operations (distance, area, buffer) use the CRS unit - EPSG:4326 unit is **degrees** — `st_buffer(x, 1000)` means 1000 degrees, not meters ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} zh <- st_sfc(st_point(c(8.54, 47.38)), crs = 4326) st_crs(zh)$ud_unit ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 1 [°] ``` ::: ::: --- ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} zh_lv95 <- st_transform(zh, 2056) st_crs(zh_lv95)$ud_unit ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 1 [m] ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} zh_lv95 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Geometry set for 1 feature Geometry type: POINT Dimension: XY Bounding box: xmin: 2683171 ymin: 1248268 xmax: 2683171 ymax: 1248268 Projected CRS: CH1903+ / LV95 ``` ::: ::: - Always check CRS before measurement; transform if needed - **Axis order trap:** everyday usage is **lat, lon** (47.38, 8.54); sf / EPSG:4326 expects **(x, y) = lon, lat** (8.54, 47.38) # GDAL and the Vector Ecosystem {.subtitle} ## GDAL: one library, many tools - [GDAL](https://gdal.org) (Geospatial Data Abstraction Library) underlies almost all GIS software: - QGIS, ArcGIS, GRASS, SAGA, FME, ... - R (`sf`) - Python (`geopandas`) - PostGIS ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # sf delegates format detection to GDAL — driver chosen from file extension stationen <- read_sf("data/uebung1/stationen_schweiz.geojson") # → GeoJSON driver hoheitsgebiet <- read_sf("data/Spatial_Analysis_I/Hoheitsgebiet/HOHEITSGEBIET_FR.shp") # → Shapefile driver ``` ::: - GDAL supports [80+ vector formats](https://gdal.org/en/latest/drivers/vector/index.html); `sf` inherits all of them ## Important Vector file formats | Format | Extension | Strengths | Limitations | |---|---|---|---| | Shapefile | `.shp` (+ 4 files) | Universal legacy support | 10-char field names; 2 GB limit; no nulls | | GeoJSON | `.geojson` | Human-readable; single file; web-native | Large files; no spatial index | | GeoPackage | `.gpkg` | Modern; single file; multiple layers; SQLite inside | Less universal than Shapefile | | PostGIS | (database) | Live DB; concurrent access; fast spatial index | Requires a server | | FlatGeobuf | `.fgb` | Very fast; streamable; built-in spatial index | Newer, less tool support | | DuckDB | `.duckdb` | Columnar analytics; spatial extension; queries remote files | Not a traditional GIS format | # Binary Predicates {.subtitle} ## Spatial relationships as questions - Binary predicates return TRUE/FALSE for a pair of geometries - The question determines the correct predicate: - *Is this building inside the flood zone?* → `st_within(building, zone)` - *Does this road cross the zone?* → `st_crosses(road, zone)` - *Does any part of this forest touch Luzern?* → `st_intersects(forest, luzern)` - The same pair can satisfy multiple predicates — wrong choice gives **silently wrong results** ## Named predicates | Predicate | | When TRUE | Typical use case | |--|:---:|-------|-------| | `intersects` | ![](images/predicates/intersects.png){width=100px} | Any overlap exists (broadest) | Initial spatial filter | | `disjoint` | ![](images/predicates/disjoint.png){width=100px} | No overlap whatsoever | Exclusion / NOT queries | | `touches` | ![](images/predicates/touches.png){width=100px} | Boundaries meet; interiors do not | Adjacent parcels, shared borders | :::{.notes} - `intersects` is almost always TRUE for non-trivial pairs — rarely the right predicate for a precise question ::: ## Named predicates | Predicate | | When TRUE | Typical use case | |--|:---:|-------|-------| | `within` | ![](images/predicates/within.png){width=100px} | All of A is inside B | Point-in-polygon, containment | | `contains` | ![](images/predicates/contains.png){width=100px} | All of B is inside A | Inverse of `within` | | `overlaps` | ![](images/predicates/overlaps.png){width=100px} | Interiors intersect; neither contains the other | Partial overlap of same-type features | | `crosses` | ![](images/predicates/crosses.png){width=100px} | Interior of A intersects interior of B in lower dimension | Road through a zone | ## Choosing the right predicate ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # intersects: any part of the forest touches Luzern (including tiny overlap at the border) wald_intersects <- st_filter(tlm_wald, luzern, .predicate = st_intersects) # within: the *entire* forest polygon lies inside Luzern wald_within <- st_filter(tlm_wald, luzern, .predicate = st_within) nrow(wald_intersects) # more: includes forests that merely touch the border ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3852 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} nrow(wald_within) # fewer: only forests completely inside ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3729 ``` ::: ::: --- ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![`st_intersects` (left) vs `st_within` (right) — same data, different predicate, different question answered](vector-data_files/figure-revealjs/fig-predicates-1.png){#fig-predicates width=960} ::: ::: # Geometry Operations {.subtitle} ## Unary operations - Take one geometry, return a (possibly different type of) geometry: | Operation | What it does | Output type | |---|---|---| | `st_buffer(x, dist)` | Expand by distance | Polygon | | `st_centroid(x)` | Center point | Point | | `st_simplify(x, tol)` | Reduce vertex count | Same type | | `st_convex_hull(x)` | Smallest convex polygon enclosing the geometry | Polygon | | `st_boundary(x)` | The boundary of the geometry | Lower dimension | ## Binary set operations - Set algebra on geometries — same logic as SQL set operations - `st_union()` on a **single layer**: dissolve / aggregate — analogous to `GROUP BY` in SQL | Operation | Returns | Set notation | |---|---|---| | `st_intersection(A, B)` | Parts where A and B overlap | A ∩ B | | `st_union(A, B)` | All of A and B, merged | A ∪ B | | `st_difference(A, B)` | Parts of A outside B | A \ B | | `st_sym_difference(A, B)` | Parts of A or B, but not both | A △ B | ## Operations can change geometry type - Output type depends on the geometry relationship, not just the operation - Intersecting two polygons can yield a polygon, a line, or a point: - Overlapping → **polygon**; - sharing only an edge → **line**; - sharing only a corner → **point** - Code expecting a polygon **fails silently** if inputs only touch --- ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} wald_clipped <- st_intersection(luzern, tlm_wald) # Fraction of Luzern covered by forest sum(st_area(wald_clipped)) / st_area(luzern) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 0.2721733 [1] ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](vector-data_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-9-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: # Group Work {.subtitle} ## Write an algorithm How do you make a Peanutbutter & Jelly Sandwitch (PB&J) ![](images/pbj.avif) ## {background-iframe="https://www.youtube.com/embed/FN2RM-CHkuI?si=u-FJbPsDpu4vIXYL" backgrond-interactive=false} ## Challenge 1: Bounding box of a point stream - A continuous stream of 2D coordinates arrives one point at a time. - **Task:** develop an algorithm for the smallest axis-aligned bounding box of all points received so far. - **Constraints**: process each point once; do not store the full list; update the box on each new point. - Example stream: ``` 2489750, 1117500 2506250, 1172500 2552750, 1223500 ... ``` :::{.callout-important title="Closed book!"} Do not use any external sources. Solve with your own ideas in groups ::: ## Challenge 2: Is a point inside a polygon? - **Given:** an ordered sequence of 2D polygon vertices and a point with known coordinates. - **Task:** develop an algorithm that determines whether the point is inside or outside the polygon. - Constraints: use only the vertex coordinates; no visual inspection; must work for arbitrary simple polygons. :::{.callout-important title="Closed book!"} Do not use any external sources. Solve with your own ideas in groups ::: ## References {#refs}

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
